map.An integers & coordinate-plane adventure: A story about integers & the coordinate plane. It has five chapters and six reader gates. Solve the math to light the city again.
map.Pattern distortion: severe. City power:: Bad pattern: very bad. City power: going out. Reader: dress warm.
map.Previously, in Volume Six: the crew forg: Last time, in Volume Six: the crew made the master key. They opened Ada Vex's vault. They shut down the sign glitch. The last page said: "When the lights go out, start at zero". Tonight, in deep winter, they did.
map.The whole grid went dark at 6:14. Jamal: The whole grid went dark at 6:14. Jamal, we lead this one. You and me. Notebook and proof.
map.Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engi: Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engine. It is at Meridian Avenue and Zero Street. That is dead center.
map.Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. T: Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. The engine sits at the origin, (0, 0). Power goes out from zero. It goes one part of town at a time.
map.East–west streets count along the x-axis: East–west streets count on the x-axis. North–south streets count on the y-axis. Where they cross is the origin.
map.Vexhall Observatory steps. The old brass: Outside Vexhall. It is cold. The old thermometer still works. Just barely.
map.Down to −8° tonight. Yesterday's high wa: It is −8° tonight. Yesterday's high was 5°. The cellar stays at −3°.
map.Below-zero numbers. Whole ones with no f: Numbers below zero. Whole ones with no fraction. So they are integers?
map.Correct. Integers: counting numbers, the: Yes. Integers are the counting numbers, their opposites, and zero. Opposites are the same distance from zero. They are on the other side. Tonight's reading is −7. The heat box wakes when it shows the opposite.
map.An integer is a whole number, its opposi: An integer is a whole number. Or its opposite. Or zero. −8, −3, 0, and 5 are all integers.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. L: Reader, you are on our crew. Log the readings. Spin the dial!
map.The heat router needs yesterday's log. P: The heat box needs the old log. Pick a reading chip. Then tap its mark on the thermometer: −8°, −3°, and 5°. Then wake the box. Its dial must show the opposite of −7. Type that number.
map.Conceptual: zero is the freezing mark. N: Conceptual: zero is the freeze mark. Negative readings are BELOW zero. The more negative, the LOWER the mark. Opposites are the same distance from zero. They are on the other side.
map.Procedural: start at 0 and count ticks D: Procedural: start at 0. Count marks DOWN for a negative reading. −3 is three marks below zero. For an opposite, keep the distance from zero. Flip the side.
map.Heater trucks roll to the coldest distri: Heat trucks go to the coldest part first. But which part IS coldest? One reading is a fraction.
map.Don't trust your eyes. Under a minus sig: Don't trust your eyes. With a minus sign, a big digit is cold.
map.All four are rational numbers — any numb: All four are rational numbers. You can write each one as a fraction. Like −2.5 or −¾. They look different. They share one number line.
map.Rational numbers include integers, fract: Rational numbers can be integers, fractions, or decimals. They can be positive or negative. Least means most far below zero.
map.Sort the ledger, reader — the coldest di: Sort the list, reader. The coldest part of town gets the first truck!
map.Four district readings: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°: Four readings: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°, −¾°. Tap the cards in order from least to greatest. Coldest goes first. Tap a card again to undo it.
map.Conceptual: colder means farther BELOW z: Conceptual: colder means more far BELOW zero. On a number line, the least is far left. With negatives, a big digit is cold.
map.Procedural: rewrite everything the same: Procedural: write them all the same way first. As a decimal, three fourths is 0.75. So −¾ = −0.75. Then go left to right on the number line.
We are in the tunnel. It is under Meridian Avenue. Samir taps the map.
map.Two relay stations on the line: W at −6,: Two stations on the line: W at −6, E at 4. Far from the engine at zero? It needs a strong boost.
map.Distance, not direction. The bars in |−6: Distance, not which way. The bars in |−6| mean absolute value. It is how far from zero. Skip the sign.
map.Absolute value is never negative. Direct: Absolute value is never negative. The sign tells which way. The bars tell the distance.
map.Absolute value |n| = a number's distance: Absolute value |n| = a number's distance from 0. |−6| asks: how many steps from zero?
map.Set the booster strengths, reader. Then: Set the boosts, reader. Then say which station is farther out.
map.Booster strength = the station's absolut: Boost = the station's absolute value. That is its distance from the engine at zero. Set both: |−6| for Station W and |4| for Station E. Then say which station is farther from zero.
map.Conceptual: absolute value bars measure: Conceptual: absolute value bars show DISTANCE from zero. Distance has no sign. |−9| and |9| are both 9.
map.Procedural: count steps from 0 to the st: Procedural: count steps from 0 to the station. Use the number line. For "farther from zero," compare the two distances. Pick the station with the bigger distance.
map.Ada's map cuts the city into four quadra: Ada's map cuts the city into four quadrants. Start top right. Go the other way from a clock: I, II, III, IV.
map.Every station is an ordered pair (x, y):: Each station is an ordered pair (x, y). First go east or west. Then go north or south. (2, 5) is NOT (5, 2).
map.Two relays must light next: (−3, 2) and: Two stations must light next: (−3, 2) and (4, −1). But my map is mixed up. Five dots blink. Just two are real.
map.An ordered pair (x, y) locates a point:: An ordered pair (x, y) shows a point. x is first (left or right). Then y (up or down).
map.Read the pairs carefully, reader. Light: Read the pairs with care, reader. Light the wrong one and we waste power.
map.Five dots flicker on Ada's map, but only: Five dots blink on Ada's map. Just the stations at (−3, 2) and (4, −1) are real. Tap to light exactly those two. Tap again to turn one off. Then name their quadrants.
map.Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). T: Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). Start at the origin. The first number moves left (negative) or right (positive). The second moves down (negative) or up (positive).
map.Procedural: walk each pair: for (−1, 4): Procedural: walk each pair. For (−1, 4), go 1 block left. Then go 4 blocks up. Quadrants go the other way from a clock. Start at top right: I, then II, then III, then IV.
map.Cable time. Even elevation runs below ze: Time for cable. Down here, even height goes below zero. The old deck is at −6 meters.
map.And cable doesn't stretch. We count exac: And cable does not stretch. We count the exact blocks between stations. No guessing.
map.Two runs tonight: across Fourth Street f: Two runs tonight. Across Fourth Street, from (−3, 4) to (5, 4). Down Second Avenue, from (2, −1) to (2, −6).
map.When two points share a coordinate, the: Two points may share a coordinate. Then the path is straight. Find its length with absolute values.
map.Measure both cable runs, reader. I cut o: Find both cable lengths, reader. I cut once.
map.Measure both cable runs in blocks. Cable: Find the length of both cables in blocks. Cable A: (−3, 4) to (5, 4). Cable B: (2, −1) to (2, −6). Count exactly. Priya cuts once.
map.Conceptual: when two points share a coor: Conceptual: two points may share a coordinate. Then the cable is straight. Check the numbers that change. On OPPOSITE sides of zero? ADD their absolute values. Same side of zero? SUBTRACT them.
map.Procedural: like (−4, 1) to (2, 1): x cr: Procedural: like (−4, 1) to (2, 1). x crosses zero, so |−4| + |2| = 6 blocks. Like (7, −2) to (7, −9). Same side, so 9 − 2 = 7 blocks.
map.Midnight. One move left: ring the engine: Midnight. One move left. Ring the engine with cable. Then the whole grid lights up again.
map.The Light Ring: a rectangle of cable thr: The Light Ring is a rectangle of cable. It has four corner stations. I can sense its shape. You must find its size.
map.Width, height, then total cable. Three l: Width, height, then all the cable. Three locks, one ring. Reader, bring us home.
map.Boss Gate: distances on the plane, plus: Boss Gate: distance on the plane. And the perimeter of a polygon on the grid.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The city is watc: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The city is watching. (The city is also freezing.)
map.The ring's corner relays: (−4, −2), (3,: The ring's corner stations: (−4, −2), (3, −2), (3, 3), (−4, 3). Open all three locks to close the ring:
map.Total cable to close the ring (perimeter: All the cable to close the ring (perimeter):
map.Conceptual: a side's length is the dista: Conceptual: look at the coordinates that CHANGE. The side length is the distance between them. On opposite sides of zero? Add the two distances. The perimeter is the trip around all four sides.
map.Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6: Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6 crosses zero: 2 + 6 = 8 blocks. Perimeter quick way: 2 × (width + height).
map.Quadrant by quadrant — look at it glow!: Quadrant by quadrant. Look at it glow!
Twenty-four blocks of cable. None left over. Led, counted, checked.
map.Achievement unlocked: city un-frozen. Ho: Level won: city not frozen. Now, hot cocoa. Fast.
map.New distortion below city hall. A door s: New bad pattern. It is under city hall. Its door looks like a balance scale. It wants things EQUAL. To be continued…
map.Crew co-captain. Keeps the notebook, ask: Crew co-boss. Keeps the notebook. Asks the next question. In this volume: called the quadrant order that lit the city.
map.Evidence officer and co-lead. This volum: Proof finder and co-lead. In this volume: used the cold to teach integers.
map.Builder and cable boss. This volume: mea: Builder and cable boss. In this volume: found each cable length with absolute values. And cut once.
map.Pattern hunter. This volume: matched sig: Pattern finder. In this volume: matched signal strength to distance from zero.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. It can sense bad patterns. It can't do math. That's your job.
map.Opposites.Same distance from zero, oppos: Opposites.Same distance from zero, opposite sides: −7 and 7. The opposite of 0 is 0.
map.Rational numbers.Any number you can writ: Rational numbers.Any number you can write as a fraction. −3, −2.5, −¾, 0.5 all share one number line. Least is the most far left.
map.Absolute value.|n| is distance from zero: Absolute value.|n| is distance from zero. It is never negative: |−6| = 6 and |4| = 4.
map.Ordered pairs & quadrants.(x, y): x move: Ordered pairs & quadrants.(x, y): x moves left–right, y up–down. The axes cut the plane into quadrants I–IV. Start top right. Go the other way from a clock.
map.Distance on the plane.Points sharing a c: Distance on the plane.Points that share a coordinate make a straight path. Opposite sides of zero → add absolute values. Same side → subtract.
map.\"Zero is not nothing. Zero is where you: "Zero is not nothing. Zero is where you stand to see both sides." — A.V.
map.completed Volume 7: Below Zero and prove: finished Volume 7: Below Zero. You know integers, opposites, and rational numbers. You know absolute value and the four quadrants. You know distance on the coordinate plane.
map.Thank you for braving the cold with the: Thank you for facing the cold with the crew. Volume 8 waits behind the balance scale door.
map.Place −6° on a thermometer: start at the: Put −6° on a thermometer. Start at the 0 mark. Count six marks down. That is −6.
map.Its opposite keeps the same distance — s: Its opposite keeps the same distance, six. But it flips the side. Six marks UP lands on 6.
map.So −6 and 6 are opposites: same distance: So −6 and 6 are opposites. Same distance from zero, opposite ways.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
Write as decimals: −1.5, 1, −0.5, −2. The most far below zero is −2. That's the least.
map.Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negati: Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negatives can fool you. Check the distance below zero.
map.|−8| = 8 steps from zero. |3| = 3 steps: |−8| = 8 steps from zero. |3| = 3 steps from zero.
map.8 > 3, so the station at −8 is farther f: 8 > 3. So the one at −8 is far from zero. But −8 is the SMALLER number.
map.x = −2 → walk two blocks LEFT. y = −5 →: x = −2 → go two blocks LEFT. y = −5 → go five blocks DOWN.
map.Left and down lands in Quadrant III — th: Left and down lands in Quadrant III. There, both signs are negative.
map.A point has positive x and negative y. W: A point has positive x and negative y. Which quadrant, 1–4?
map.Measure (−6, 3) to (3, 3): the y-values: Find (−6, 3) to (3, 3). The y-values match. So the run goes sideways.
map.x goes from −6 to 3 — opposite sides of: x goes from −6 to 3. Opposite sides of zero. So add the distances: |−6| + |3| = 9 blocks.
map.Now (4, −1) to (4, −7): both y-values ar: Now (4, −1) to (4, −7). Both y-values are below zero. Same side. So subtract: 7 − 1 = 6 blocks.
map.Width: x runs from −1 to 3, crossing zer: Width: x goes from −1 to 3. It crosses zero → 1 + 3 = 4. Height: y goes from −2 to 1 → 2 + 1 = 3.
map.A grid rectangle is 6 wide and 3 tall. H: A grid rectangle is 6 wide and 3 tall. How much cable goes around it?
map.Place all three readings on the thermome: Put all three readings on the thermometer first. Tap a chip, then a mark.
map.A negative reading lives BELOW the zero: A negative reading is BELOW the zero mark. Check which side of 0 your mark is on.
map.−8 is COLDER than −3 — deeper below zero: −8 is COLDER than −3. It is more below zero. So its mark is LOWER.
map.At least one reading sits on the wrong t: At least one reading is on the wrong mark. Count marks from 0 with care.
map.Readings logged, dial at 7 — the heat ro: Readings logged. The dial is at 7. The heat box hums awake!
map.Readings placed! Now the dial: an opposi: Readings placed! Now the dial. An opposite keeps the distance from zero. It flips the side.
Tap all four readings. Coldest first.
−3 < −2.5 < −¾ < 0.5. Frostvale first. Heat trucks roll out. The coldest part goes first!
map.Careful — −¾ is only ¾ below zero. −2.5: Look again. −¾ is just ¾ below zero. −2.5 is two and a half below. Colder goes lower.
map.Not coldest-to-warmest yet. Picture all: Not coldest to warmest yet. Think of all four on a number line. Then tap.
map.Distance is never negative — drop the si: Distance is never negative. Drop the sign in the bars.
map.Absolute value asks: how many steps from: Absolute value asks: how many steps from 0? Count them on the line.
map.Strengths are set… now compare the two d: The boosts are set. Now compare the two distances you found. Which one is bigger?
map.Boosters set: 6 and 4. Station W at −6 s: Boosts set: 6 and 4. Station W at −6 is farther from zero. It gets the big boost. Signal is back!
map.Check the signs: in (−3, 2), the −3 mean: Check the signs. Look at (−3, 2). The −3 means 3 blocks LEFT of the engine, not right.
map.The second number is the up–down move: (: The second number moves up or down. (−3, 2) goes UP 2. It does not go down.
map.Re-walk each pair from the origin: left–: Walk each pair from the origin again. Left–right first, then up–down.
map.Relays lit! Now the quadrants — count co: Lit! Now the quadrants. Start at top right. Go the other way from a clock: I, II, III, IV.
map.(−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II and (4, −1): (−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II. (4, −1) glows in Quadrant IV. The stations link up!
map.Cable A crosses x = 0 — don't subtract s: Cable A crosses x = 0. Don't just subtract across zero. Add each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Cable A runs sideways: only the x-number: Cable A goes sideways. Just the x numbers change. Count the blocks between them.
map.Both y-values sit on the SAME side of ze: The y-values are on the SAME side. Subtract the small distance from the big one.
map.Cable B runs up–down: only the y-numbers: Cable B goes up and down. Just the y numbers change. Count with care below zero.
map.8 blocks across, 5 blocks down — both ca: 8 blocks across, 5 blocks down. Both cables cut just right!
map.Lock 1 holds. Width: x runs from −4 to 3: Lock 1 is shut. Width: x goes from −4 to 3. Those are opposite sides of zero. So ADD each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Lock 2 holds. Height: y runs from −2 up: Lock 2 is shut. Height: y goes from −2 up to 3. Opposite sides again. Add the distances.
map.Lock 3 holds. 35 is the AREA inside the: Lock 3 is shut. 35 is the AREA inside the ring. The cable goes around the EDGE. Add all four sides.
map.Lock 3 holds. That's one width plus one: Lock 3 is shut. That's one width and one height. The ring needs BOTH widths and BOTH heights.
map.Lock 3 holds. Perimeter is the whole tri: Lock 3 is shut. Perimeter is the whole trip around: width + height + width + height.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable close: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable close the ring. The Light Ring glows. Axiom City lights up, quadrant by quadrant!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
map.Walk the steps above again — you've got: Go through the steps above again. You can do it.
